headline: Venezuela earthquake death toll climbs to 1,500 as rescue efforts intensify
summary: Two devastating earthquakes have left a trail of destruction, with thousands injured and displaced. Rescue teams are working tirelessly amid aftershocks, hoping to find more survivors.
details: The death toll from two devastating earthquakes in Venezuela has risen to approximately 1,500. Rescue workers, both local and international, are working day and night to free people still trapped under the rubble.

The coastal state of La Guaira, located about 40 kilometers north of the capital Caracas, is the most severely affected area. Hundreds of buildings have collapsed there, with authorities confirming 774 structures completely destroyed so far.

Interim President Delcy Rodriguez stated that rescue operations will continue as there is still a possibility of finding survivors. The government has formed a special commission to determine if damaged buildings are habitable, and educational institutions in La Guaira will remain closed for another week.

According to government figures, 3,150 people have been injured and 12,721 displaced. At least 33 people were rescued alive by Saturday evening, including a father and his son pulled from a collapsed building on Sunday.
Meanwhile, an opposition-backed website claims that nearly 50,000 people are still missing. Ongoing aftershocks are making the rescue operations even more challenging for the teams on the ground.

According to government figures, 3,150 people have been injured and 12,721 displaced. At least 33 people were rescued alive by Saturday evening, including a father and his son pulled from a collapsed building on Sunday.

headline_marked: [[Passenger seriously injured by stone pelting on train]] in Brahmanbaria again
headline: Passenger seriously injured by stone pelting on train in Brahmanbaria again
summary: A passenger sustained serious injuries after stones were pelted at a train in Brahmanbaria. This marks another incident of such violence in the area.
details: A train passenger was seriously injured after stones were thrown at the train in Brahmanbaria. This incident highlights a recurring problem of stone pelting on trains in the region.
The victim sustained severe injuries and required immediate medical attention. Authorities are urged to address the persistent issue to ensure passenger safety.
Stone pelting incidents on trains have been reported multiple times in Brahmanbaria. Such acts pose significant risks to passengers and railway staff, causing both physical harm and property damage.
Investigations into this latest incident are expected to be launched by railway police. Measures to prevent future occurrences are crucial for the safety and security of commuters.
